_about: Standard tests per category. See backend/category_tests.py.

apple_cider_vinegar.name: Acidity (acetic acid strength)
apple_cider_vinegar.why: Brewed vinegar must have at least 3.75% acetic acid; a lower figure means it has been watered down.
apple_cider_vinegar.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.46(1)(a)(i) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_3_Fruit_Vegetable_products.pdf; Unbox Health tests

apple_cider_vinegar.name: Real brewed vinegar: total solids, ash, no mineral acid
apple_cider_vinegar.why: Fake 'apple cider' vinegar is often diluted synthetic acetic acid; real brewed vinegar has fruit solids and ash, and must never contain sulphuric or other mineral acid.
apple_cider_vinegar.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.46(1)(a)(ii)-(iv) (total solids ≥1.5%, total ash ≥0.18%, no mineral acid, not fortified with acetic acid) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_3_Fruit_Vegetable_products.pdf

apple_cider_vinegar.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
apple_cider_vinegar.why: Acidic vinegar can pull lead and other metals out of equipment and containers; FSSAI's lead limit for vinegar is very strict (0.01 ppm).
apple_cider_vinegar.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1.1 (brewed & synthetic vinegar: lead 0.01, copper 0.01, arsenic 0.1 ppm) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

apple_cider_vinegar.name: Added colour (only caramel allowed)
apple_cider_vinegar.why: Vinegar may only be coloured with caramel; other dyes are used to make cheap vinegar look like apple cider vinegar.

ashwagandha_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
ashwagandha_supplement.why: Withanolides are the active compounds, and cheap extracts are often well below the claimed percentage.
ashwagandha_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 and FAQ 73 https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests total withanolides (8 reports)

ashwagandha_supplement.name: Withaferin-A (leaf use check)
ashwagandha_supplement.why: High withaferin-A suggests ashwagandha leaves were used; FSSAI and AYUSH have banned leaves in food products over safety concerns.
ashwagandha_supplement.source: FSSAI advisory on non-use of ashwagandha leaves, Apr 2026 https://fssai.gov.in/upload/advisories/2026/04/69e0d84fcac2fAdvisory%20on%20non%20use%20of%20ashwagandha%20leaves%20in%20crude%20or%20extract%20or%20any%20other%20form%20in%20food%20products-%20reg.pdf; Unbox Health tests (4 reports)

ashwagandha_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
ashwagandha_supplement.why: Herb roots grown in contaminated soil can carry lead and arsenic, a known problem in Ayurvedic products.
ashwagandha_supplement.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India limits for herbal material (lead 10, arsenic 3, cadmium 0.3, mercury 1 ppm); FSSAI Nutra FAQ 73 (pharmacopoeial purity criteria) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

ashwagandha_supplement.name: Pesticide residues
ashwagandha_supplement.why: Farmed herb roots can carry pesticide residues.
ashwagandha_supplement.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India pesticide residue limits for herbal material

ashwagandha_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
ashwagandha_supplement.why: Dried root powder comes from the soil and can carry germs if not cleaned and treated.
ashwagandha_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

astaxanthin.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
astaxanthin.why: Astaxanthin is very expensive and degrades with light and air, so under-dosing is common.
astaxanthin.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

astaxanthin.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
astaxanthin.why: Algae-sourced astaxanthin can absorb heavy metals from its growth water.
astaxanthin.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

astaxanthin.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
astaxanthin.why: Algae-derived ingredients and capsules must be free of germs.
astaxanthin.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

berberine_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
berberine_supplement.why: Berberine is a strong blood-sugar-lowering compound, so the real dose matters for both effect and safety.
berberine_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

berberine_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
berberine_supplement.why: Root and bark extracts can carry lead and arsenic from soil.
berberine_supplement.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India limits for herbal material (lead 10, arsenic 3, cadmium 0.3, mercury 1 ppm); FSSAI Nutra FAQ 73 (pharmacopoeial purity criteria) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

berberine_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
berberine_supplement.why: Herbal powders and capsules can carry germs from the field.
berberine_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

biotin_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
biotin_supplement.why: Biotin doses vary hugely between brands, and very high doses can upset blood test results, so the real amount matters.
biotin_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

biotin_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
biotin_supplement.why: Tablets and gummies can carry heavy metals from fillers.
biotin_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

biotin_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
biotin_supplement.why: Hair gummies are sugary and can grow germs if made badly.
biotin_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

biscuits.name: Nutrition vs label claims
biscuits.why: Biscuits are often marketed as 'digestive', 'high fibre' or 'sugar free'; tests check sugar, fat and fibre against the label.

biscuits.name: Trans fat (FSSAI 2% of fat limit)
biscuits.why: Biscuits are made with vanaspati and bakery shortenings, the main source of trans fat that raises heart-disease risk.
biscuits.source: FSSAI trans fat limit (industrial TFA ≤2% of fat, products made from 1 Jan 2022) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/advisories/2021/12/61c0659e591e2Letter_Compliance_Trans_Fat_20_12_2021.pdf

biscuits.name: Rancidity (acid value, peroxide value)
biscuits.why: Old or poor-quality fat in biscuits goes rancid; FSSAI caps acidity of extracted fat at 2%.
biscuits.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.15(1) biscuits https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf; Consumer Voice biscuit tests

biscuits.name: Purity: ash insoluble in HCl
biscuits.why: Acid-insoluble ash above 0.1% means sand or grit in the flour.
biscuits.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.15(1) biscuits https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf; Consumer Voice biscuit tests

biscuits.name: Aflatoxins
biscuits.why: Aflatoxins from mouldy flour, nuts or groundnut survive baking.
biscuits.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (total aflatoxins 15 µg/kg, B1 10 µg/kg in cereals; 20 µg/kg in products containing them); Unbox Health biscuit tests

biscuits.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
biscuits.why: Metals from flour, cocoa and water carry into biscuits that children eat a lot of.
biscuits.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits); Unbox Health biscuit tests

biscuits.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
biscuits.why: Cream-filled biscuits handled after baking can pick up E. coli and other bacteria.
biscuits.source: Consumer Voice biscuit tests (total plate count, E. coli)

bread.name: Potassium bromate / iodate
bread.why: A 2016 CSE study found these possibly cancer-causing flour improvers in most Indian breads; FSSAI then banned bromate.
bread.source: CSE bread study 2016 and FSSAI ban https://www.cseindia.org/bread-study-outcome-cse-welcomes-fssais-ban-on-potassium-bromate-6472; Consumer Voice bread tests

bread.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
bread.why: Bread is eaten without further cooking and goes mouldy quickly; Salmonella and Listeria must be absent and mould counts low.
bread.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B Table 9A/9B (bread: Salmonella and Listeria absent/25 g) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf; Consumer Voice and Unbox Health tests

bread.name: Nutrition vs label claims
bread.why: Checks fibre, protein and sugar against the label, especially on 'brown', 'whole wheat' or 'multigrain' breads.

bread.name: Purity: alcoholic acidity, ash insoluble in HCl
bread.why: High alcoholic acidity means stale or poorly made bread, and high acid-insoluble ash means grit in the flour.
bread.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.15(2) bread https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf; Consumer Voice bread tests

bread.name: Aflatoxins
bread.why: Aflatoxins from mouldy wheat survive baking.
bread.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (total aflatoxins 15 µg/kg, B1 10 µg/kg in cereals; 20 µg/kg in products containing them); Unbox Health bread tests

bread.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
bread.why: Metals from flour and water carry into bread, which many people eat daily.
bread.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits); Unbox Health bread tests

breakfast_cereal.name: Nutrition vs label claims
breakfast_cereal.why: Breakfast cereals sold to children are often high in sugar and claim added iron and vitamins; tests check both against the label.

breakfast_cereal.name: Purity: moisture, ash insoluble in HCl, alcoholic acidity
breakfast_cereal.why: Too much moisture makes cereal soggy and mouldy, and high acid-insoluble ash or alcoholic acidity means grit or stale grain.
breakfast_cereal.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.35 breakfast cereal (moisture ≤7.5%/10%, AIA ≤0.1%) and 2.4.8 corn flakes https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf

breakfast_cereal.name: Aflatoxins
breakfast_cereal.why: Maize and other grains in cereals are prone to aflatoxin-producing moulds.
breakfast_cereal.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (total aflatoxins 15 µg/kg, B1 10 µg/kg in cereals; 20 µg/kg in products containing them); Unbox Health and Trustified tests

breakfast_cereal.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
breakfast_cereal.why: Grains, cocoa and rice in cereals can carry lead, arsenic and cadmium.
breakfast_cereal.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits); Unbox Health and Consumer Voice tests

breakfast_cereal.name: Pesticide residues
breakfast_cereal.why: Oats, maize and wheat are sprayed crops and residues can carry into the cereal.

breakfast_cereal.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
breakfast_cereal.why: Cereal is eaten without cooking, so Salmonella and Listeria must be absent.
breakfast_cereal.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B Table 9B (other ready-to-eat grain products: Salmonella, Listeria absent/25 g) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf; Consumer Voice tests

butter.name: Milk fat, moisture and salt (vs FSSAI standard)
butter.why: Too much water or salt means less butter for your money; FSSAI requires at least 80% milk fat, at most 16% moisture and 3% salt.
butter.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.9 (table butter); Consumer Voice tests

butter.name: Purity: BR reading, RM value (foreign fat check)
butter.why: These tests on the extracted fat catch butter cut with vegetable oil or vanaspati.
butter.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.9 (extracted fat to meet ghee RM/BR values); Consumer Voice tests

butter.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
butter.why: Butter made from unpasteurised or badly handled cream can carry coliforms, moulds and Listeria.
butter.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B; Consumer Voice tests

butter.name: Acidity (lactic acid)
butter.why: High acidity points to sour, old cream and gives off-flavours.

butter.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
butter.why: Metals from contaminated milk or equipment accumulate in the body over time.
butter.source: FSSAI CTR Regs 2011 (compendium): https://jaivikbharat.fssai.gov.in/pdf/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations.pdf (Reg 2.1 metal limits); Consumer Voice lead test

butter.name: Pesticide residues
butter.why: Fat-loving pesticides from cattle feed concentrate in milk fat, so butter carries more than milk.
butter.source: FSSAI CTR Regs 2011 (compendium): https://jaivikbharat.fssai.gov.in/pdf/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations.pdf (Reg 2.3: pesticide limits for milk products on a fat basis); Trustified tests

calcium_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
calcium_supplement.why: Calcium tablets are often short on elemental calcium, and many also claim vitamin D that needs checking.
calcium_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

calcium_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
calcium_supplement.why: Calcium from shells, bone or mined carbonate is a well-known source of lead.
calcium_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

calcium_supplement.name: Tablet breakdown (disintegration / dissolution)
calcium_supplement.why: A tablet that does not break down in the stomach passes through without releasing its nutrients, whatever the label says.
calcium_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 72 (tablets/capsules must meet IP/BP/USP quality standards) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; USP Dietary Supplement Verification Program

cheese.name: Moisture and milk fat (dry-matter basis)
cheese.why: Extra water or low milk fat means you're getting less cheese than the variety name promises.
cheese.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.17 (cheese and cheese products composition table) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Draft_WTO_SPS_Notification_Standards_Diary_26_04_2018.pdf

cheese.name: Analogue check (vegetable fat, starch)
cheese.why: 'Cheese analogue' made with vegetable oil and starch is sold in place of real cheese, especially on pizzas; Maharashtra banned analogue cheese in 2026.
cheese.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.1/2.1.17 (cheese only from milk); Trustified beta-sitosterol test; Maharashtra FDA 2026 ban: https://ianslive.in/maharashtra-fda-bans-analog-cheese-and-artificial-paneer-for-one-year-after-legislative-push--20260805103420

cheese.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
cheese.why: Soft and fresh cheeses are a classic source of Listeria, which is dangerous in pregnancy.

cheese.name: Aflatoxin M1 (from mouldy cattle feed)
cheese.why: Aflatoxin M1 binds to casein, so cheese can carry several times the level of the milk it was made from.
cheese.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (Aflatoxin M1 in milk 0.5 µg/kg); Trustified tests

cheese.name: Nutrition vs label claims
cheese.why: Cheese is high in salt and saturated fat, so the label's sodium and fat figures matter.
cheese.source: FSSAI Labelling & Display Regs 2020 (nutrition declaration); Unbox/Trustified-style label checks

chips.name: Nutrition vs label claims
chips.why: Chips are high in fat and salt, and 'baked' or 'healthy' variants make fat and sodium claims that need checking.

chips.name: Trans fat (FSSAI 2% of fat limit)
chips.why: Chips fried in partially hydrogenated oil can carry trans fat, which raises heart-disease risk.
chips.source: FSSAI trans fat limit (industrial TFA ≤2% of fat) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/advisories/2021/12/61c0659e591e2Letter_Compliance_Trans_Fat_20_12_2021.pdf; Unbox Health chips tests

chips.name: Rancidity (acid value, peroxide value)
chips.why: Oil in chips oxidises and goes rancid over shelf life, especially in packs that let in light or air.
chips.source: Consumer Voice fried snack tests; FSSAI FPS Reg 2.12.1 proprietary food https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/13_%20Chapter%202_12%20(Proprietary%20Food).pdf

chips.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
chips.why: Potatoes and other root crops pick up cadmium and lead from soil.
chips.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits); Unbox Health chips tests

chocolate.name: Cocoa solids & milk solids vs FSSAI standard
chocolate.why: Cheap chocolate cuts cocoa and milk solids below FSSAI's minimums (e.g. milk chocolate ≥2.5% cocoa solids, ≥10.5% milk solids).
chocolate.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.7.4 chocolate https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_7%20(Sweets%20and%20Confectionary).pdf; Consumer Voice chocolate tests

chocolate.name: Vegetable fat (non-cocoa fat ≤5%)
chocolate.why: Cocoa butter is replaced with cheaper vegetable fats; FSSAI allows at most 5% and requires a label declaration.
chocolate.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.7.4(1) and 5(b) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_7%20(Sweets%20and%20Confectionary).pdf; Consumer Voice chocolate tests (melting point)

chocolate.name: Nutrition vs label claims
chocolate.why: Checks sugar, fat and energy against the label.

chocolate.name: Synthetic colours
chocolate.why: Coloured and coated chocolates can contain non-permitted or excess synthetic colours.
chocolate.source: Consumer Voice chocolate tests (synthetic food colour)

chocolate.name: Purity: ash insoluble in HCl
chocolate.why: Acid-insoluble ash above 0.2% means grit or poor-quality cocoa.
chocolate.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.7.4 chocolate https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_7%20(Sweets%20and%20Confectionary).pdf; Consumer Voice chocolate tests

chocolate.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
chocolate.why: Cocoa takes up cadmium and lead from soil and drying, so chocolate can carry heavy metals.
chocolate.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead in cocoa powder 5.0 mg/kg fat-free dry basis)

cocoa_powder.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
cocoa_powder.why: Cocoa powder concentrates the cadmium and lead in cocoa beans; FSSAI caps lead at 5 mg/kg.
cocoa_powder.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (cocoa powder: lead 5.0, copper 70 mg/kg on fat-free dry basis)

cocoa_powder.name: Purity: cocoa butter, ash insoluble in HCl, alkalinity, added colour
cocoa_powder.why: Cocoa powder bulked with husk or coloured fillers fails FSSAI's limits for cocoa butter, acid-insoluble ash and ash alkalinity, and added colour isn't allowed.

cocoa_powder.name: Aflatoxins
cocoa_powder.why: Cocoa beans dried in damp conditions can grow aflatoxin-producing moulds.

cocoa_powder.name: Pesticide residues
cocoa_powder.why: Cocoa is a heavily sprayed crop and residues carry into the powder.
cocoa_powder.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3.1; Trustified cocoa powder tests

coffee_powder.name: Purity: caffeine, ash, chicory and fillers
coffee_powder.why: Coffee is bulked up with chicory, roasted husk, tamarind or date seed and even clay; low caffeine and high ash give it away, and 'pure coffee' must have no chicory at all.
coffee_powder.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.10.2 (roasted & ground: caffeine ≥1.0%, total ash 3–6%, acid-insoluble ash ≤0.1%; soluble: caffeine ≥2.8%, no chicory) and 2.10.4 (coffee ≥51% in coffee-chicory) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_10_BEVERAGES_Other%20than%20Dairy%20and%20Fruits%20Vegetables%20based.pdf; FSSAI DART (chicory, clay in coffee) https://www.fssai.gov.in/book-details.php?bkid=201; Unbox Health tests

coffee_powder.name: Ochratoxin A
coffee_powder.why: Badly dried or stored coffee beans grow moulds that make ochratoxin A, which can harm the kidneys; FSSAI set a 5 µg/kg limit for coffee from April 2025.
coffee_powder.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 as amended 17.10.2024, effective 01.04.2025 (ochratoxin A: coffee 5 µg/kg) https://taxguru.in/?p=935564; Unbox Health tests

coffee_powder.name: Aflatoxins
coffee_powder.why: Mouldy beans can also carry aflatoxins, which damage the liver.
coffee_powder.source: Unbox Health tests (total aflatoxins in 8 coffee reports)

coffee_powder.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
coffee_powder.why: Coffee can pick up lead, arsenic and copper from soil, sprays and roasting/grinding equipment.
coffee_powder.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1.1 (copper: coffee beans 30 ppm; foods not specified lead 2.5 ppm) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

coffee_powder.name: Pesticide residues
coffee_powder.why: Coffee is a sprayed crop and FSSAI sets residue limits for several pesticides on it.
coffee_powder.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3.1 (coffee MRLs, e.g. copper fungicides, others) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf

collagen_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
collagen_supplement.why: Collagen peptides per serving are often less than claimed.
collagen_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

collagen_supplement.name: Collagen identity (hydroxyproline, glycine, proline)
collagen_supplement.why: Real collagen is rich in hydroxyproline, glycine and proline; a low score means cheaper protein has been passed off as collagen.
collagen_supplement.source: Unbox Health collagen panel (hydroxyproline, glycine, proline and % of amino acids)

collagen_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
collagen_supplement.why: Collagen made from animal hides and bones can concentrate lead and other metals.
collagen_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

collagen_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
collagen_supplement.why: Collagen is an animal by-product powder and must be free of germs like Salmonella.
collagen_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

cooking_oil.name: Purity: refractive index, iodine value, saponification value (blending check)
cooking_oil.why: Each oil has a fixed chemical fingerprint; values outside FSSAI's range mean it was cut with a cheaper oil. Oil-specific extras: Bellier test (groundnut), Polenske value (coconut), oryzanol (rice bran, min 1%), HCN test (mustard).
cooking_oil.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.2.1 (per-oil standards) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_2_Fats_oil_fat%20emulsions.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

cooking_oil.name: Rancidity (acid value, peroxide value)
cooking_oil.why: Oxidised, stale oil has high acid and peroxide values, tastes off and forms harmful compounds; FSSAI caps peroxide at 10 meq/kg for refined oils.
cooking_oil.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.2.1 (acid value per oil) and 2.2.8 (peroxide value) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_2_Fats_oil_fat%20emulsions.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

cooking_oil.name: Argemone and mineral oil (toxic adulterant oils)
cooking_oil.why: Argemone seed oil causes epidemic dropsy and is mostly found mixed into mustard oil; mineral oil is a cheap non-food filler. FSSAI requires both to be absent in all oils.
cooking_oil.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.2.1 (test for argemone oil negative; free from mineral oil) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_2_Fats_oil_fat%20emulsions.pdf; FSSAI DART / Check Adulteration at Home: https://fssai.gov.in/cms/checkadulteration.php

cooking_oil.name: Trans fat and fatty acid profile (vs label)
cooking_oil.why: FSSAI limits trans fat to 2% since 2022, and labels claim MUFA/PUFA/saturated levels (multi-source oils must stay under 33% saturated).
cooking_oil.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.2.1(16) (refined oil trans fat ≤2%) and 2.2.1(24) (multi-source oil) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_2_Fats_oil_fat%20emulsions.pdf; Consumer Voice and Unbox tests

cooking_oil.name: Hexane residue (solvent-extracted oils)
cooking_oil.why: Refined and solvent-extracted oils (sunflower, rice bran, soybean, refined groundnut/mustard) can retain hexane solvent; FSSAI allows at most 5 ppm and none in pressed oils.
cooking_oil.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.2.1 (hexane ≤5.0 ppm in refined oils) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_2_Fats_oil_fat%20emulsions.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

cooking_oil.name: Aflatoxins
cooking_oil.why: Mould toxins from damaged seeds, mainly a risk in groundnut and unrefined oils, can damage the liver.
cooking_oil.source: FSSAI CTR Regs 2011 (compendium): https://jaivikbharat.fssai.gov.in/pdf/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations.pdf (Reg 2.2.1: aflatoxin in oilseeds/oil 10-15 µg/kg); Consumer Voice and Unbox tests

cooking_oil.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
cooking_oil.why: Metals from soil or processing equipment can carry into oil; FSSAI caps lead in edible oils at 0.1 ppm.
cooking_oil.source: FSSAI CTR Regs 2011 (compendium): https://jaivikbharat.fssai.gov.in/pdf/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations.pdf (Reg 2.1: lead 0.1 mg/kg in edible oils); Consumer Voice and Unbox tests

coq10_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
coq10_supplement.why: CoQ10 is expensive and breaks down with light, so products often contain less than the label says.
coq10_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

coq10_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
coq10_supplement.why: Capsules and their oil carriers can carry heavy metals.
coq10_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

coq10_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
coq10_supplement.why: Capsules and tablets can pick up germs in manufacturing.
coq10_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

creatine_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
creatine_supplement.why: Creatine is cheap to under-dose or cut with fillers, so the real creatine per scoop is the core check.
creatine_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

creatine_supplement.name: Creatine purity (creatinine, dicyandiamide, dihydrotriazine)
creatine_supplement.why: Poorly made creatine can contain manufacturing by-products (dicyandiamide, dihydrotriazine) and breakdown product creatinine that does nothing for you.
creatine_supplement.source: USP Creatine Monohydrate monograph impurity tests (USP-grade spec: DCD <=50 ppm, DHT not detectable); supplier COAs

creatine_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
creatine_supplement.why: Imported creatine bulk and fillers can carry heavy metals into a product taken every day.
creatine_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests all four (10 reports)

curcumin_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
curcumin_supplement.why: Curcuminoids are the active compounds, and many products fall short of the claimed 95%.
curcumin_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests total curcuminoids (6 reports); Food Chemistry 2021 study: only 4 of 14 met label

curcumin_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
curcumin_supplement.why: Turmeric is India's best-known lead problem (lead chromate added for colour), and extracts can carry it through.
curcumin_supplement.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India limits for herbal material (lead 10, arsenic 3, cadmium 0.3, mercury 1 ppm); FSSAI Nutra FAQ 73 (pharmacopoeial purity criteria) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

curcumin_supplement.name: Piperine (black pepper extract) vs label
curcumin_supplement.why: Piperine is added to boost curcumin absorption; too little means the claimed benefit is not there.
curcumin_supplement.source: Unbox Health tests total piperine (6 reports)

curcumin_supplement.name: Synthetic curcumin check
curcumin_supplement.why: Cheaper lab-made curcumin is sold as 'natural turmeric extract'; an unusual curcuminoid ratio gives it away.
curcumin_supplement.source: Eurofins case study, Food Chemistry 2021 (HPLC curcuminoid ratio + carbon-14) https://www.nutraceuticalsworld.com/exclusives/identifying-adulterated-curcumin-case-study-identifies-best-testing-method/

curcumin_supplement.name: Pesticide residues
curcumin_supplement.why: Turmeric is a farmed crop and its extracts can carry pesticide residues.
curcumin_supplement.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3 (spices); Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India limits

curd.name: Nutrition vs label claims
curd.why: Curd made from cheaper, thinner milk carries less fat, protein and calcium than the pack says.
curd.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1 (dahi: fat/SNF as for the milk used); Consumer Voice tests

curd.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
curd.why: Fermented foods made in unhygienic conditions can carry coliforms, moulds or pathogens like Listeria and Salmonella.
curd.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B (fermented milk products)

curd.name: Acidity (lactic acid)
curd.why: Too much acid means the curd is old or over-fermented; too little means it wasn't properly cultured.
curd.source: Consumer Voice tests; FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1 (fermented milk products, titratable acidity)

curd.name: Vegetable fat or starch (non-milk thickeners)
curd.why: Curd must be made only from milk; palm oil or starch added for body cheats buyers and can't be seen by eye.
curd.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.1 (general standard: milk products only from milk); FSSAI DART / Check Adulteration at Home: https://fssai.gov.in/cms/checkadulteration.php (starch iodine test); Trustified beta-sitosterol test

curd.name: Aflatoxin M1 (from mouldy cattle feed)
curd.why: The liver-damaging toxin from mouldy feed passes from milk into curd.
curd.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (Aflatoxin M1 in milk 0.5 µg/kg); Trustified tests

dairy_whitener.name: Milk protein, fat and added sugar (vs standard and label)
dairy_whitener.why: Whitener can be padded with sugar or low-protein solids; FSSAI caps added sucrose at 18% and requires milk protein of at least 34% of non-fat solids.
dairy_whitener.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.11 (dairy whitener); Consumer Voice tests

dairy_whitener.name: Moisture and acid-insoluble ash
dairy_whitener.why: Too much moisture lets the powder cake and spoil; acid-insoluble ash flags sand or dirt.
dairy_whitener.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.11 (moisture max 4%); Consumer Voice tests

dairy_whitener.name: Solubility and acidity (insolubility index)
dairy_whitener.why: Powder that won't dissolve or is too acidic is old, heat-damaged or badly stored.
dairy_whitener.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.10 (milk powders: insolubility index, titratable acidity); Consumer Voice tests

dairy_whitener.name: Melamine
dairy_whitener.why: Melamine has been used to fake protein in milk powder (China 2008, which killed infants); FSSAI caps it at 2.5 mg/kg.
dairy_whitener.source: FSSAI CTR Regs 2011 (compendium): https://jaivikbharat.fssai.gov.in/pdf/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations.pdf (Reg 2.5.1: melamine 2.5 mg/kg in other foods)

dairy_whitener.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
dairy_whitener.why: Powders made or packed in poor hygiene can carry Salmonella and other bacteria that survive drying.
dairy_whitener.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B (dried milk products); Consumer Voice tests

dairy_whitener.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
dairy_whitener.why: Drying concentrates any metals in the milk, and FSSAI applies the milk lead limit with a concentration factor.
dairy_whitener.source: FSSAI CTR Regs 2011 (compendium): https://jaivikbharat.fssai.gov.in/pdf/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations.pdf (Reg 2.1: lead in milks, concentration factor for dried milks)

dark_chocolate.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
dark_chocolate.why: Consumer Reports found lead and cadmium in all 28 dark chocolate bars it tested in 2022; more cocoa means more metal.
dark_chocolate.source: Consumer Reports 2022 https://www.npr.org/2022/12/17/1143239430/dark-chocolate-lead-cadmium-consumer-reports; FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead in cocoa powder 5.0 mg/kg); Unbox Health tests

dark_chocolate.name: Cocoa solids vs label %
dark_chocolate.why: Dark chocolate must have at least 35% total cocoa solids under FSSAI; the '70%' on the label should match what's inside.
dark_chocolate.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.7.4(4)(iii) (dark chocolate ≥35% cocoa solids, ≥18% cocoa butter) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_7%20(Sweets%20and%20Confectionary).pdf; Unbox Health tests

dark_chocolate.name: Nutrition vs label claims
dark_chocolate.why: Checks sugar and fat against the label, since dark chocolate is sold as the healthier choice.

dark_chocolate.name: Vegetable fat (non-cocoa fat ≤5%)
dark_chocolate.why: Cocoa butter is swapped for cheaper vegetable fats; FSSAI allows at most 5% with a label declaration.

dark_chocolate.name: Aflatoxins
dark_chocolate.why: Cocoa beans fermented and dried in warm, damp conditions can grow toxin-producing moulds.

electrolyte.name: Nutrition vs label claims
electrolyte.why: Sodium, potassium and chloride are the whole point of an electrolyte mix, and they need to match the label to rehydrate properly.
electrolyte.source: FSSAI Labelling & Display Regs 2020; Unbox Health tests sodium, potassium, chloride

electrolyte.name: Sugar content
electrolyte.why: High-sugar 'electrolyte' drinks can worsen dehydration; FSSAI barred non-WHO-formula drinks from using the ORS name in Oct 2025.

electrolyte.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
electrolyte.why: Mineral salts used in electrolyte mixes can carry lead and arsenic.
electrolyte.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1; Unbox Health tests all four

electrolyte.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
electrolyte.why: Ready-to-drink electrolytes are sold for sick and dehydrated people, so they must be free of germs.

fibre_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
fibre_supplement.why: Fibre powders can be bulked with cheaper fillers, giving less fibre per spoon than claimed.
fibre_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

fibre_supplement.name: Purity: swell volume, total ash, acid-insoluble ash, moisture
fibre_supplement.why: Low swelling or high ash means the husk is old, impure or mixed with sand and dirt, so it works poorly.
fibre_supplement.source: FSSAI draft isabgol husk standard (swell volume >=40 ml/g, acid-insoluble ash <=0.45%, ash <=4.0%, moisture <=11.5%) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Draft_Notice_Comments_Nutraceuticals_11_04_2018.pdf; Trustified tests these

fibre_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
fibre_supplement.why: Plant husks soak up lead and cadmium from soil, and you take them daily.
fibre_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

fibre_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
fibre_supplement.why: Husk and plant fibre come from the field and can carry germs like Salmonella if not cleaned properly.
fibre_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

flour.name: Purity: ash insoluble in HCl, alcoholic acidity, uric acid, gluten
flour.why: Sand or soil, stale or insect-damaged grain show up as high acid-insoluble ash, alcoholic acidity and uric acid (insect excreta), and low gluten in atta and maida means a poor or diluted flour.
flour.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.1 (atta), 2.4.2 (maida), 2.4.4 (besan) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf; FSSAI DART test 19

flour.name: Aflatoxins
flour.why: Mould on badly stored wheat or gram makes aflatoxins, which damage the liver and can cause cancer; flour is eaten every day so small amounts add up.
flour.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (total aflatoxins 15 µg/kg, B1 10 µg/kg in cereals; 20 µg/kg in products containing them)

flour.name: Pesticide residues
flour.why: Wheat and chana are sprayed in the field and in storage, and residues can carry into the flour.
flour.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.6(1) (food grains must meet CTR Reg 2.3.1 MRLs); Consumer Voice and Trustified tests

flour.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
flour.why: Grain picks up lead and cadmium from soil, water and mills, and these build up in the body over years.
flour.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits) (lead 0.2 mg/kg cereal grains, cadmium 0.2 mg/kg wheat); Consumer Voice atta tests (lead)

flour.name: Added colour or khesari dal (besan)
flour.why: Besan is sometimes coloured yellow or bulked with cheap khesari dal, which can cause paralysis (lathyrism); FSSAI bans both.
flour.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.4 (besan: no added colouring) and 2.4.6(1) (grains free from kesari) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf; FSSAI DART test 14

flour.name: Nutrition vs label claims
flour.why: Checks that protein and fibre (e.g. on multigrain or high-fibre atta) match what the pack says.

ghee.name: Purity: BR reading, RM value, Baudouin test
ghee.why: These are FSSAI's core checks that ghee is pure milk fat and not cut with vanaspati or vegetable oil (the Baudouin test catches the sesame oil marker in vanaspati).
ghee.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.8 (milk fat products: ghee); Consumer Voice tests

ghee.name: Foreign fat (vegetable oil, animal body fat)
ghee.why: Ghee is faked with palm oil or other fats; the 2024 Tirupati laddu ghee was later found to be mostly palm oil and palm kernel oil. Sterol and fatty-acid tests catch this.
ghee.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.8 (beta-sitosterol absent; fatty acid composition added by 6th Amendment 2021, in force 27.12.2023); Tirupati case: https://www.deccanherald.com/amp/story/india%2Fandhra-pradesh%2Ftirumala-laddu-row-cbi-finds-ghee-was-vegetable-oil-not-animal-fat-rs-234-crore-scam-unearthed-3879229

ghee.name: Rancidity (acid value, peroxide value)
ghee.why: Old or badly stored ghee goes rancid; high free fatty acids and peroxides mean stale fat and off-flavour.
ghee.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.8 (FFA limit); Consumer Voice tests

ghee.name: Moisture
ghee.why: Ghee should be almost water-free (max 0.5%); extra water adds weight and makes it spoil faster.
ghee.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.8; Consumer Voice tests

ghee.name: Nutrition vs label claims
ghee.why: Ghee labels state saturated fat, trans fat, cholesterol and vitamin A, which should match the product.
ghee.source: Consumer Voice and Unbox Health tests

ghee.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
ghee.why: Lead from contaminated milk or processing equipment builds up in the body over time.
ghee.source: FSSAI CTR Regs 2011 (compendium): https://jaivikbharat.fssai.gov.in/pdf/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations.pdf (Reg 2.1 metal limits); Unbox Health tests

glucose_powder.name: Glucose (dextrose) content
glucose_powder.why: The product is sold as instant energy from glucose; testing shows whether it is mostly dextrose or cheaper sugars and fillers.
glucose_powder.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.8.5 (dextrose: glucose ≥99.0% on dry basis) and 2.8.7 (dried glucose syrup) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_8%20(Sweetening%20agents%20including%20Honey).pdf; Consumer Voice tests (dextrose equivalent)

glucose_powder.name: Nutrition vs label claims
glucose_powder.why: Glucose drinks advertise added calcium, phosphorus and vitamin D; testing checks those claims and the calorie count.
glucose_powder.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.12.1 proprietary food (vitamins/minerals ≤1 RDA); FSS (Labelling & Display) Regulations 2020; Consumer Voice tests

glucose_powder.name: Purity: sulphated ash and acidity
glucose_powder.why: High ash or acidity means poorly refined glucose or added mineral fillers.
glucose_powder.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.8.5 (sulphated ash ≤0.1% dry basis, acidity limit) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_8%20(Sweetening%20agents%20including%20Honey).pdf

glucose_powder.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
glucose_powder.why: Refined dextrose should be almost metal-free; FSSAI caps lead in dextrose at 0.5 ppm.
glucose_powder.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1.1 (anhydrous dextrose & dextrose monohydrate: lead 0.5 ppm) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf

granola.name: Nutrition vs label claims
granola.why: Granola is sold as a health food; tests check sugar, fibre and protein claims against the label.

granola.name: Aflatoxins
granola.why: Oats, nuts and dried fruit in granola are all prone to aflatoxin-producing moulds.
granola.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (total aflatoxins 15 µg/kg, B1 10 µg/kg in cereals; 20 µg/kg in products containing them) and nuts 15 µg/kg; Unbox Health tests

granola.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
granola.why: Oats, seeds and cocoa can carry lead, cadmium and arsenic.
granola.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits); Unbox Health tests

granola.name: Rancidity (acid value, peroxide value)
granola.why: Granola is baked with oil and nuts, which go rancid over its shelf life; FSSAI requires breakfast cereals to be free from rancid taste.
granola.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.35(5) breakfast cereals (covers granola) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf

granola.name: Purity: moisture, ash insoluble in HCl
granola.why: Too much moisture lets mould grow, and high acid-insoluble ash means grit; FSSAI's breakfast cereal standard explicitly covers granola.
granola.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.35 breakfast cereal (moisture ≤10% with fruit/nuts, AIA ≤0.1%) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf

granola.name: Pesticide residues
granola.why: Oats and other grains are sprayed crops and residues can carry into the mix.
granola.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3.1; Trustified breakfast cereal tests

granola.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
granola.why: Granola is eaten uncooked, often with cold milk, so Salmonella and Listeria must be absent.
granola.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B Table 9B (other ready-to-eat grain products) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf

health_drink.name: Nutrition vs label claims
health_drink.why: These powders are sold on protein, vitamin and mineral claims; testing shows whether the pack delivers them.
health_drink.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.11 (malted milk food: protein ≥12.5%/11.25%, fat ≥7.5%/6%) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf; FSSAI Reg 2.12.1 proprietary food (vitamins/minerals ≤1 RDA); Consumer Voice tests

health_drink.name: Sugar content
health_drink.why: Many 'health drinks' are largely sugar; after a 2024 probe into Bournvita's sugar the government told e-commerce sites to stop listing them as health drinks.
health_drink.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.11 (malted milk food without cocoa may not contain added sugar); Commerce Ministry advisory 10.04.2024 after NCPCR probe https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/india/health-drink-not-defined-under-norms-remove-bournvita-from-category-centre-610476; Consumer Voice tests

health_drink.name: Quality: moisture, acid-insoluble ash, solubility
health_drink.why: High moisture spoils the powder, acid-insoluble ash means sand or dirt, and poor solubility suggests added starch or fillers.
health_drink.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.11 (moisture ≤5%, acid-insoluble ash ≤0.1%, solubility ≥85%/80%, starch test negative, alcoholic acidity ≤0.30%) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

health_drink.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
health_drink.why: Milk and cereal powders can carry Salmonella or E. coli if made or packed unhygienically.
health_drink.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.11 (bacterial count ≤50,000/g, coliform ≤10/g, Salmonella, E. coli absent) and Appendix B Table 9 (malted milk food) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf; Consumer Voice tests

health_drink.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
health_drink.why: Cocoa, cereals and added minerals can bring lead and cadmium into the powder.
health_drink.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1.1 (cocoa powder lead 5 ppm; foods not specified 2.5 ppm) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf

health_drink.name: Aflatoxins
health_drink.why: Milk powder and malted grains can carry aflatoxin M1/B1 from mouldy feed or grain.
health_drink.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (aflatoxin M1 in milk powders; total aflatoxin in cereal products 15 µg/kg) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf

honey.name: Sugar syrup adulteration (C4/C3 sugars, rice syrup marker)
honey.why: Cheap cane, corn or rice syrups are mixed into honey to bulk it up, and many big Indian brands have been caught doing it.
honey.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.8.3 (C4 sugar max 7%, Δδ13C, 2-AFGP rice-syrup marker absent, foreign oligosaccharides, pollen count) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_8%20(Sweetening%20agents%20including%20Honey).pdf; CSE NMR investigation Dec 2020 (10 of 13 brands failed); Consumer Voice & Unbox Health tests

honey.name: Purity: moisture, HMF, sucrose, fructose/glucose ratio, diastase
honey.why: These show whether honey is real, fresh and unheated: high HMF or sucrose, low diastase or an odd fructose/glucose ratio point to added sugar, overheating or old stock.
honey.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.8.3 (moisture ≤20%, reducing sugars ≥65%, sucrose ≤5%, F/G 0.95–1.50, HMF ≤80 mg/kg, diastase ≥3, proline ≥180) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_8%20(Sweetening%20agents%20including%20Honey).pdf; Consumer Voice & Unbox Health tests

honey.name: Antibiotic residues (chloramphenicol, nitrofurans, tetracyclines)
honey.why: Beekeepers sometimes dose hives with antibiotics, which are banned in honey and leave residues you then eat.
honey.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3.2(3) (antibiotics in honey, LC-MS/MS limits; tightened by Oct 2024 amendment) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; https://taxguru.in/?p=935564

honey.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
honey.why: Honey can pick up lead and other metals from processing equipment, storage drums and polluted foraging areas.
honey.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1.1 ('foods not specified' limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

hyaluronic_acid_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
hyaluronic_acid_supplement.why: Hyaluronic acid is costly, so products are often short on it or rely on cheaper fillers.
hyaluronic_acid_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

hyaluronic_acid_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
hyaluronic_acid_supplement.why: Fermentation- or animal-sourced HA and capsule fillers can carry heavy metals.
hyaluronic_acid_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

hyaluronic_acid_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
hyaluronic_acid_supplement.why: Fermentation-made or animal-tissue ingredients must be free of germs.
hyaluronic_acid_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

ice_cream.name: Ice cream vs frozen dessert (milk fat vs vegetable fat)
ice_cream.why: Only milk-fat products may be called ice cream; cheaper 'frozen desserts' use vegetable oil and are sometimes passed off as ice cream.
ice_cream.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1 (ice cream) and 2.1.15 (frozen dessert); FSSAI myth-buster: https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Myth%20buster%20on%20Ice%20cream%20and%20frozen%20dessert%20.pdf

ice_cream.name: Total solids, fat and protein (vs ice cream standard)
ice_cream.why: Ice cream pumped with air and water has fewer solids; FSSAI requires at least 36% total solids for full ice cream.
ice_cream.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1 (ice cream composition); Unbox Health tests

ice_cream.name: Nutrition vs label claims
ice_cream.why: Sugar and calorie figures on ice cream packs are what most buyers check, so they should be accurate.

ice_cream.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
ice_cream.why: Ice cream is a known source of Listeria and Salmonella when mix is under-pasteurised or the cold chain breaks.
ice_cream.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B (ice cream / frozen confections)

ice_cream.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
ice_cream.why: Metals can come from milk, colours or equipment; FSSAI also caps tin in ice cream at 1 ppm.
ice_cream.source: FSSAI CTR Regs 2011 (compendium): https://jaivikbharat.fssai.gov.in/pdf/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations.pdf (Reg 2.1: tin in ice-cream 1.0 mg/kg); Unbox Health tests

ice_cream.name: Melamine
ice_cream.why: Melamine can enter through adulterated milk powder used in the mix; FSSAI caps it at 2.5 mg/kg.
ice_cream.source: FSSAI CTR Regs 2011 (compendium): https://jaivikbharat.fssai.gov.in/pdf/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations.pdf (Reg 2.5.1); Unbox Health tests

idli_dosa_batter.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
idli_dosa_batter.why: Fresh batter is a wet, fermenting food handled in small units; FSSAI sets Staphylococcus aureus and Enterobacteriaceae limits because dirty handling or water shows up here.
idli_dosa_batter.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B Table 9A (batters and doughs, ready to cook: S. aureus and Enterobacteriaceae) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf

idli_dosa_batter.name: Nutrition vs label claims
idli_dosa_batter.why: Checks that protein, carbs and sodium match the pack label.

idli_dosa_batter.name: Aflatoxins
idli_dosa_batter.why: Rice and urad dal stored badly can carry aflatoxins into the batter.
idli_dosa_batter.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (total aflatoxins 15 µg/kg, B1 10 µg/kg in cereals; 20 µg/kg in products containing them) and pulses 15 µg/kg; Unbox Health tests

idli_dosa_batter.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
idli_dosa_batter.why: Rice and dal pick up lead, cadmium and arsenic from soil and water.
idli_dosa_batter.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits); Unbox Health tests

infant_formula.name: Nutrition vs label claims
infant_formula.why: Babies rely on formula as their only food, so protein, fat, vitamins, minerals and DHA must match the label and the legal minimums.
infant_formula.source: FSS (Foods for Infant Nutrition) Regulations 2020, composition tables and DHA 0.2–0.5% of fatty acids if claimed https://www.thc.nic.in/Central%20Governmental%20Regulations/Food%20Safety%20and%20Standards%20(Foods%20for%20Infant%20Nutrition)%20Regulations,%202020.pdf

infant_formula.name: Microbiology (Cronobacter, Salmonella, Bacillus cereus)
infant_formula.why: Powdered formula is not sterile; Cronobacter and Salmonella in it can cause deadly infections in newborns.
infant_formula.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B Table 2B (infant formula: Salmonella, Listeria, B. cereus, Cronobacter, Enterobacteriaceae) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf; FSS (Foods for Infant Nutrition) Reg 2020 cl. (12) https://www.thc.nic.in/Central%20Governmental%20Regulations/Food%20Safety%20and%20Standards%20(Foods%20for%20Infant%20Nutrition)%20Regulations,%202020.pdf

infant_formula.name: Melamine
infant_formula.why: Melamine was added to fake protein in formula in the 2008 China scandal; FSSAI caps it at 1 mg/kg in infant formula powder.
infant_formula.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.5.1 (melamine: powdered infant formula 1.0 mg/kg, liquid 0.15 mg/kg) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; Trustified tests

infant_formula.name: Aflatoxins
infant_formula.why: Aflatoxin M1 passes from mouldy cattle feed into milk powder, and infants are the most vulnerable to it.
infant_formula.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (aflatoxin M1 in milk powders) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; Trustified tests (aflatoxins B1, B2, G1, G2, M1)

infant_formula.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
infant_formula.why: Even small amounts of lead or arsenic harm a baby's developing brain; FSSAI limits are much stricter for infant foods.
infant_formula.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1.1 (infant formula ready-to-use lead 0.02 ppm; infant milk substitutes lead 0.2, arsenic 0.05, cadmium 0.1 ppm) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf

infant_formula.name: Pesticide residues
infant_formula.why: Pesticides in milk or cereal ingredients carry over into formula, where babies eat it every day.
infant_formula.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3.1 (0.01 mg/kg default where no MRL set) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; Foods for Infant Nutrition Reg 2020 cl. (10) https://www.thc.nic.in/Central%20Governmental%20Regulations/Food%20Safety%20and%20Standards%20(Foods%20for%20Infant%20Nutrition)%20Regulations,%202020.pdf; Trustified tests

instant_noodles.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
instant_noodles.why: In 2015 FSSAI ordered Maggi off shelves after state labs reported lead above limits; lead harms children's brain development.
instant_noodles.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits); Maggi 2015 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maggi_noodles_safety_concerns_in_India; Consumer Voice and Unbox Health tests

instant_noodles.name: Nutrition vs label claims
instant_noodles.why: Noodles and their tastemaker are very high in sodium and refined carbs; tests check these against the label.
instant_noodles.source: Consumer Voice and Unbox Health noodle tests

instant_noodles.name: Rancidity (acid value, peroxide value)
instant_noodles.why: Fried noodles hold a lot of oil that goes rancid; FSSAI caps acid value at 2.0 for fried noodles.
instant_noodles.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.10(2) instant noodles https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf; Consumer Voice noodle tests

instant_noodles.name: Trans fat (FSSAI 2% of fat limit)
instant_noodles.why: Fried noodles use palm or hydrogenated oils that can carry trans fat.
instant_noodles.source: FSSAI trans fat limit (industrial TFA ≤2% of fat, products made from 1 Jan 2022) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/advisories/2021/12/61c0659e591e2Letter_Compliance_Trans_Fat_20_12_2021.pdf

instant_noodles.name: Purity: moisture, ash insoluble in HCl
instant_noodles.why: FSSAI caps moisture (10% fried, 13% non-fried) and acid-insoluble ash (0.3%), which flags grit and poor drying.
instant_noodles.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.10(2) instant noodles https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf; Consumer Voice noodle tests

instant_noodles.name: Aflatoxins
instant_noodles.why: Aflatoxins from mouldy wheat flour carry into the noodles.
instant_noodles.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (total aflatoxins 15 µg/kg, B1 10 µg/kg in cereals; 20 µg/kg in products containing them); Consumer Voice noodle tests

instant_noodles.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
instant_noodles.why: Noodle cakes and seasoning must be free of Salmonella.
instant_noodles.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B Table 9B (instant noodles: Salmonella absent/25 g) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf

iron_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
iron_supplement.why: Iron doses need to be right: too little won't fix anaemia and too much causes stomach upset and, in children, poisoning.
iron_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

iron_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
iron_supplement.why: Iron salts can carry lead and arsenic from raw materials.
iron_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

iron_supplement.name: Tablet breakdown (disintegration / dissolution)
iron_supplement.why: A tablet that does not break down in the stomach passes through without releasing its nutrients, whatever the label says.
iron_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 72 (tablets/capsules must meet IP/BP/USP quality standards) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; USP Dietary Supplement Verification Program

jaggery_powder.name: Purity: sucrose, reducing sugars, ash insoluble in HCl
jaggery_powder.why: Jaggery mixed with refined sugar, chalk or grit fails FSSAI's limits for sucrose (≥70%), reducing sugars and acid-insoluble ash.
jaggery_powder.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.8.4(2) cane jaggery https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_8%20(Sweetening%20agents%20including%20Honey).pdf; Unbox Health tests

jaggery_powder.name: Chalk and added colour
jaggery_powder.why: Jaggery is bulked with chalk powder or coloured to look golden, and FSSAI does not allow any added colour.
jaggery_powder.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.8.4(2)(2) (added colour not permitted) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_8%20(Sweetening%20agents%20including%20Honey).pdf; FSSAI DART test 9

jaggery_powder.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
jaggery_powder.why: Jaggery boiled in metal pans and made from cane grown on contaminated soil can carry lead and other metals.
jaggery_powder.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1; FSSAI FPS Reg 2.8.4(2)(4); Unbox Health tests

jam.name: Fruit & sugar content: TSS, fruit %, pectin
jam.why: A jam must be at least 45% fruit and 65% soluble solids; low readings mean it is mostly sugar syrup, thickener and flavour.
jam.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.31(6)-(7) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_3_Fruit_Vegetable_products.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

jam.name: Preservatives (benzoic acid, sulphur dioxide)
jam.why: Benzoate and sulphite are allowed only up to set limits; overuse can trigger allergies and asthma in sensitive people.
jam.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix A, category 4.1.2.5 (jams) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20A(4).pdf; Consumer Voice tests

jam.name: Mould and yeast
jam.why: Jam must show no mould growth or fermentation; high mould or yeast counts mean poor hygiene or spoilage.
jam.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.31(10) and Appendix B (fruit products) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf; Consumer Voice tests

jam.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
jam.why: Lead and tin can leach into jam from cans, lids and processing equipment; FSSAI caps lead in jam at 1.0 ppm and tin at 250 ppm.
jam.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1.1 (lead: jams 1.0 ppm; tin: jams 250 ppm) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; Consumer Voice 'Metallic contaminants (Pb, As, Sn, Cu)'

jam.name: Nutrition vs label claims
jam.why: Checks that the sugar and calorie numbers on the label match what is in the jar.
jam.source: FSS (Labelling & Display) Regulations 2020; Consumer Voice tests

juice.name: Real juice content: TSS, acidity, vitamin C
juice.why: Low soluble solids, acidity or vitamin C mean the 'juice' is mostly water, sugar and flavouring; nectars must have 20–40% juice and fruit drinks only 10%.
juice.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.6 (fruit-wise min °Brix, max acidity, added sweetener ≤50 g/kg), 2.3.9 (nectar min juice %), 2.3.10 (fruit drink ≥10% juice) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_3_Fruit_Vegetable_products.pdf; FSSAI direction 03.06.2024 removing '100% fruit juice' claims; Consumer Voice tests

juice.name: Added synthetic colour
juice.why: Dyes make diluted juice look like fresh fruit; FSSAI's additive list for fruit juices permits no synthetic colours.
juice.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix A, category 14.1.2.1 (fruit juices: no synthetic colours listed) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20A(4).pdf; Consumer Voice tests

juice.name: Nutrition vs label claims
juice.why: Juice can be very sugary; the label must show sugar honestly and say 'sweetened juice' if more than 15 g/kg sugar is added.
juice.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.6(8) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_3_Fruit_Vegetable_products.pdf; FSS (Labelling & Display) Regulations 2020; Consumer Voice tests

juice.name: Patulin (apple juice mould toxin)
juice.why: Juice made from rotten apples can carry patulin, a mould toxin FSSAI caps at 50 µg/kg in apple juice.
juice.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (patulin: apple juice and apple juice as ingredient 50 µg/kg) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf

juice.name: Preservatives (benzoic acid, sulphur dioxide)
juice.why: Benzoate and sulphite are allowed only up to set limits; overuse can trigger asthma and allergies.
juice.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix A, category 14.1.2.1 (benzoates 1000 mg/kg, sulphites 50 mg/kg) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20A(4).pdf

juice.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
juice.why: Lead and tin can leach from cans and equipment; FSSAI caps lead in ready-to-drink juice at 0.05 ppm.
juice.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1.1 (fruit juices incl. nectars: lead 0.05 ppm; juice arsenic 0.2, copper 5, tin 250 ppm) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf

juice.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
juice.why: Poorly pasteurised juice can carry germs that cause food poisoning.
juice.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B (pasteurised & non-thermally processed juices: Salmonella, Listeria, E. coli, yeast & mould) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf

ketchup.name: Tomato content: TSS, lycopene, acidity
ketchup.why: Ketchup needs at least 25% tomato-derived solids; low lycopene or solids mean it is padded with starch, sugar and water.
ketchup.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.27 (TSS ≥25% salt-free, acidity as acetic acid) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_3_Fruit_Vegetable_products.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

ketchup.name: Added synthetic colour
ketchup.why: Dye is used to make watery, low-tomato ketchup look rich red; FSSAI's additive list for ketchup allows no synthetic colours.
ketchup.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix A, category 12.6.2 (non-emulsified sauces incl. ketchup: only natural colours like beta-carotene, paprika listed) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20A(4).pdf; Consumer Voice tests

ketchup.name: Preservatives (benzoic acid, sulphur dioxide)
ketchup.why: Preservatives are allowed only up to set limits; overuse can cause reactions in sensitive people.
ketchup.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix A, category 12.6.2 https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20A(4).pdf; Consumer Voice tests

ketchup.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
ketchup.why: Tomato concentrates and cans can carry lead, copper and tin; FSSAI caps copper in ketchup at 50 ppm.
ketchup.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1.1 (lead: processed tomato concentrates 1.5 ppm; copper: tomato ketchup 50 ppm; tin 250 ppm) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

ketchup.name: Mould and yeast
ketchup.why: High mould, yeast or bacteria counts mean rotten tomatoes or poor hygiene went into the bottle.
ketchup.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.27(2) and Appendix B (fruit & vegetable products) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf; Consumer Voice tests

ketchup.name: Nutrition vs label claims
ketchup.why: Ketchup is high in sugar and salt, so the label numbers should be accurate.
ketchup.source: FSS (Labelling & Display) Regulations 2020; Consumer Voice tests (salt as NaCl, total sugar, energy)

kids_nutrition_drink.name: Nutrition vs label claims
kids_nutrition_drink.why: These drinks are bought for their protein, vitamin, DHA and mineral claims, so testing shows whether the pack delivers them.
kids_nutrition_drink.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.12.1 proprietary food / Reg 2.4.11 malt-based food; FSS (Labelling & Display) Regulations 2020; Unbox Health tests

kids_nutrition_drink.name: Protein spiking (amino acids)
kids_nutrition_drink.why: Cheap amino acids like glycine can be added so a basic nitrogen test reads more protein than is really there.
kids_nutrition_drink.source: Trustified tests (amino spiking status); FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.11 (protein measured as N x 6.25)

kids_nutrition_drink.name: Melamine
kids_nutrition_drink.why: Melamine has been added to milk powders to fake protein readings; FSSAI caps it at 2.5 mg/kg in foods.
kids_nutrition_drink.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.5.1 (melamine: other foods 2.5 mg/kg) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; Trustified tests

kids_nutrition_drink.name: Aflatoxins
kids_nutrition_drink.why: Milk powder can carry aflatoxin M1 from mouldy cattle feed, and cereals can carry aflatoxin B1; children are especially sensitive.
kids_nutrition_drink.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (aflatoxin M1 in milk powders; cereal products) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; Trustified & Unbox Health tests

kids_nutrition_drink.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
kids_nutrition_drink.why: Lead and cadmium in cocoa, cereals and mineral premixes harm children's development.
kids_nutrition_drink.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1.1 https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

kids_nutrition_drink.name: Pesticide residues
kids_nutrition_drink.why: Pesticides in milk and cereal ingredients carry over into a drink children have every day.

kids_nutrition_drink.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
kids_nutrition_drink.why: Milk-based powders can carry Salmonella or E. coli if made or packed unhygienically.
kids_nutrition_drink.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B (milk powders; malted milk food Table 9) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf; Reg 2.4.11 microbiological limits https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf

magnesium_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
magnesium_supplement.why: Magnesium products often contain less elemental magnesium than claimed, or a cheaper form than advertised.
magnesium_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

magnesium_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
magnesium_supplement.why: Mined magnesium salts can carry lead and arsenic.
magnesium_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

magnesium_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
magnesium_supplement.why: Powders and gummies can pick up germs in manufacturing.
magnesium_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

marine_collagen.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
marine_collagen.why: Collagen peptides per serving are often less than claimed.
marine_collagen.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

marine_collagen.name: Collagen identity (hydroxyproline, glycine, proline)
marine_collagen.why: Real collagen is rich in hydroxyproline, glycine and proline; a low score means cheaper protein has been passed off as collagen.
marine_collagen.source: Unbox Health collagen panel (hydroxyproline, glycine, proline and % of amino acids)

marine_collagen.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
marine_collagen.why: Fish skin and scales can carry mercury and arsenic from the sea.
marine_collagen.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (fish limits for mercury); Unbox Health tests all four (5 reports)

marine_collagen.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
marine_collagen.why: Fish-derived powder must be free of germs like Salmonella and Listeria.
marine_collagen.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

mass_gainer.name: Nutrition vs label claims
mass_gainer.why: Gainers are mostly sugar and maltodextrin, so the real protein, carb and sugar per serving is what you are paying for.
mass_gainer.source: Citizens Protein Project, Medicine 2024 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10994440/; same protein-label testing as protein powders (Trustified, Unbox Health)

mass_gainer.name: Amino spiking (free amino acids, non-protein nitrogen)
mass_gainer.why: Cheap amino acids like glycine or taurine can be added to fool the standard nitrogen test into showing more protein than is really there.
mass_gainer.source: Trustified (41 reports) and Labdoor (free amino acids) test it; Kjeldahl/Dumas protein methods measure nitrogen, not protein

mass_gainer.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
mass_gainer.why: Large daily servings of powder add up any lead or cadmium in the ingredients.
mass_gainer.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1; FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf

mass_gainer.name: Aflatoxins
mass_gainer.why: Gainers are built on milk powder, oats and grain carbs, all of which can carry mould toxins.
mass_gainer.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2; Citizens Protein Project https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10994440/

mass_gainer.name: Banned substances (steroids, WADA-listed stimulants)
mass_gainer.why: Gym products have been caught with hidden steroids or stimulants that are unsafe and can get athletes banned.
mass_gainer.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 39 (no hormones, steroids, psychotropics) and FAQ 47 (no WADA-prohibited substances in sports foods) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf

mass_gainer.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
mass_gainer.why: A high-sugar, milk-based powder lets germs grow if made or stored badly.
mass_gainer.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

meat.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
meat.why: Raw and frozen meat can carry Salmonella, Listeria and E. coli; FSSAI requires Salmonella to be absent.
meat.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B Table 5A/5B (meat and meat products) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf; FSSAI FPS Reg 2.5.2

meat.name: Antibiotic residues
meat.why: A CSE study found antibiotic residues in 40% of chicken samples; residues fuel drug-resistant infections, and FSSAI bans drugs like nitrofurans and chloramphenicol in meat.
meat.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3.2 (banned antibiotics/veterinary drugs in meat and poultry); CSE 'Antibiotics in chicken' 2014 https://www.downtoearth.org.in/health/hatching-superbugs-45547

meat.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
meat.why: Animals accumulate lead and cadmium from feed and water, especially in offal.
meat.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits) (lead 0.1 mg/kg in meat of cattle, sheep, pig and poultry)

meat.name: Rancidity (acid value, peroxide value)
meat.why: Frozen meat stored too long or thawed and refrozen goes rancid.
meat.source: Trustified meat tests (Kreis test for rancidity)

meat.name: Pesticide residues
meat.why: Pesticides in animal feed end up in meat fat; FSSAI sets meat-specific residue limits.
meat.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3.1 (meat and poultry MRLs); Trustified meat tests

meat.name: Synthetic colours
meat.why: Marinated and processed meats are sometimes coloured red with synthetic dyes to look fresher.

melatonin_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
melatonin_supplement.why: Melatonin doses are often far off the label; a 2023 US study found gummies with 74% to 347% of the stated amount.
melatonin_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Cohen et al., JAMA 2023;329(16):1401 (melatonin gummies); Unbox Health tests (11 reports)

melatonin_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
melatonin_supplement.why: Tablets and gummies can carry heavy metals from fillers.
melatonin_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

melatonin_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
melatonin_supplement.why: Gummies and sprays are sugary or watery and can grow germs if made badly.
melatonin_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

milk.name: Milk fat and SNF (vs milk type and label)
milk.why: Watered-down or skimmed milk sold as toned/full-cream shows up as low fat or solids-not-fat, so you pay for nutrition you don't get.
milk.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.2 (milk composition table, fat/SNF by class); Consumer Voice tests. https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Draft_WTO_SPS_Notification_Standards_Diary_26_04_2018.pdf

milk.name: Adulterants (detergent, urea, starch, neutralisers, formalin, melamine)
milk.why: Detergent, urea, caustic soda, formalin or melamine are added to fake thickness, freshness or protein and can be directly harmful.
milk.source: FSSAI DART / Check Adulteration at Home: https://fssai.gov.in/cms/checkadulteration.php; FSSAI National Milk Quality Survey 2018 (https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Report_Milk_Survey_NMQS_Final_18_10_2019.pdf); Consumer Voice adulteration tests

milk.name: Aflatoxin M1 (from mouldy cattle feed)
milk.why: Cows eating mouldy feed pass this liver-damaging toxin into milk; it was the top safety failure in FSSAI's national milk survey (5.7% of samples).
milk.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (Aflatoxin M1 in milk: 0.5 µg/kg); https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Report_Milk_Survey_NMQS_Final_18_10_2019.pdf

milk.name: Antibiotic residues
milk.why: Milk from cattle treated with antibiotics can carry residues that drive antibiotic resistance; it was the second-biggest failure in FSSAI's milk survey.
milk.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3.2 (tolerance limits for antibiotics/veterinary drugs in milk, amended 2018 & 2024); https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Report_Milk_Survey_NMQS_Final_18_10_2019.pdf

milk.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
milk.why: Poor handling or failed pasteurisation lets disease-causing bacteria grow in milk.
milk.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B (microbiological standards for milk and milk products); Consumer Voice tests

milk.name: Pasteurisation check (phosphatase test)
