milk.why: A positive phosphatase test means milk sold as pasteurised wasn't heated properly, so germs may survive.
milk.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.2 (pasteurised milk, phosphatase test negative); Consumer Voice tests

milk.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
milk.why: Metals from contaminated water, feed or equipment build up in the body; FSSAI caps lead in milk at 0.02 ppm.
milk.source: FSSAI CTR Regs 2011 (compendium): https://jaivikbharat.fssai.gov.in/pdf/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations.pdf (Reg 2.1: lead 0.02, arsenic 0.1 mg/kg in milk); Consumer Voice tests

milk_thistle_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
milk_thistle_supplement.why: Silymarin is the active part of milk thistle and extracts are often below the claimed percentage.
milk_thistle_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

milk_thistle_supplement.name: Aflatoxins
milk_thistle_supplement.why: Milk thistle seeds are prone to mould, and its supplements have been found among the most mycotoxin-contaminated herbal products.
milk_thistle_supplement.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2; Veprikova et al., Toxins 2015 (mycotoxins in plant-based supplements; milk thistle highest)

milk_thistle_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
milk_thistle_supplement.why: Herbal seed extracts can carry lead and cadmium from soil.
milk_thistle_supplement.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India limits for herbal material (lead 10, arsenic 3, cadmium 0.3, mercury 1 ppm); FSSAI Nutra FAQ 73 (pharmacopoeial purity criteria) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

milk_thistle_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
milk_thistle_supplement.why: Herbal powders and capsules can carry germs from the field.
milk_thistle_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

moringa_supplement.name: Pesticide residues
moringa_supplement.why: Moringa leaf is a farmed crop; Unbox Health found pesticides above limits in moringa products.
moringa_supplement.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3; Unbox Health 'Pesticides Above Limit' (3 reports)

moringa_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
moringa_supplement.why: Leafy plants soak up lead and cadmium from soil.
moringa_supplement.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia limits; Unbox Health tests all four

moringa_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
moringa_supplement.why: Moringa is sold on its calcium, iron, vitamin and protein content, which varies widely and is often overstated.
moringa_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

moringa_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
moringa_supplement.why: Dried leaf powder can carry soil and handling germs like E. coli and Salmonella.
moringa_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

msm_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
msm_supplement.why: Joint products with MSM, glucosamine and chondroitin are often short on the costly ingredients.
msm_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

msm_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
msm_supplement.why: Glucosamine from shellfish and chondroitin from cartilage can carry heavy metals.
msm_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

msm_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
msm_supplement.why: Animal-sourced joint ingredients must be free of germs.
msm_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

muesli.name: Nutrition vs label claims
muesli.why: Muesli is sold as a health food; tests check sugar, fibre and protein claims against the label.

muesli.name: Aflatoxins
muesli.why: Oats, nuts and dried fruit in muesli are all prone to aflatoxin-producing moulds.
muesli.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (total aflatoxins 15 µg/kg, B1 10 µg/kg in cereals; 20 µg/kg in products containing them) and nuts 15 µg/kg; Unbox Health tests

muesli.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
muesli.why: Oats, seeds and cocoa can carry lead, cadmium and arsenic.
muesli.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits); Unbox Health tests

muesli.name: Purity: moisture, ash insoluble in HCl
muesli.why: Too much moisture lets mould grow, and high acid-insoluble ash means grit; FSSAI's breakfast cereal standard explicitly covers muesli.
muesli.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.35 breakfast cereal (moisture ≤10% with fruit/nuts, AIA ≤0.1%) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf

muesli.name: Pesticide residues
muesli.why: Oats and other grains are sprayed crops and residues can carry into the mix.
muesli.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3.1; Trustified breakfast cereal tests

muesli.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
muesli.why: Muesli is eaten uncooked, often with cold milk, so Salmonella and Listeria must be absent.
muesli.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B Table 9B (other ready-to-eat grain products) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf

multivitamin.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
multivitamin.why: Multivitamins often fall short on some vitamins or minerals, or overshoot safe limits on others like vitamin A, D or iron.
multivitamin.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (-10% tolerance) and FAQ 23 (overage limits, Schedule I Table C) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests vitamins A, B9, B12, D and minerals

multivitamin.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
multivitamin.why: Mineral salts in multivitamins are a known route for lead and arsenic.
multivitamin.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

multivitamin.name: Tablet breakdown (disintegration / dissolution)
multivitamin.why: A tablet that does not break down in the stomach passes through without releasing its nutrients, whatever the label says.
multivitamin.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 72 (tablets/capsules must meet IP/BP/USP quality standards) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; USP Dietary Supplement Verification Program

multivitamin.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
multivitamin.why: Tablets, gummies and capsules can pick up germs from poor manufacturing.
multivitamin.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

nuts.name: Aflatoxins
nuts.why: Groundnuts, almonds and pistachios are among the foods most prone to aflatoxin-producing moulds, which damage the liver.
nuts.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (nuts: total aflatoxins 15 µg/kg, B1 10 µg/kg); Trustified nut tests

nuts.name: Rancidity (acid value, peroxide value)
nuts.why: Nuts are high in oil and go rancid with age and heat; FSSAI caps free fatty acid and peroxide value for cashews.
nuts.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.47(7) cashew kernels (FFA ≤1.25%, peroxide value ≤10 meq/kg) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_3_Fruit_Vegetable_products.pdf

nuts.name: Pesticide residues
nuts.why: Nut crops are sprayed, and residues stay on kernels.
nuts.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3.1; Trustified nut tests

nuts.name: Quality: moisture, damaged kernels, foreign matter
nuts.why: Damp nuts grow mould, and damaged, insect-eaten kernels or foreign matter mean a poor grade.
nuts.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.47 nuts and raisins (groundnut, pistachio, almond, cashew) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_3_Fruit_Vegetable_products.pdf

nuts.name: Added colour
nuts.why: Nuts and dried fruit are sometimes coloured to look fresher, which FSSAI does not allow.
nuts.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.47 (groundnut kernels, raisins, dates free from added colouring matter) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_3_Fruit_Vegetable_products.pdf

omega_3_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
omega_3_supplement.why: EPA and DHA are the costly part of fish oil and are often under the labelled amount.
omega_3_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests EPA, DHA, ALA, total omega-3 (27-29 reports); GOED monograph

omega_3_supplement.name: Rancidity (peroxide value, anisidine, TOTOX)
omega_3_supplement.why: Fish oil goes rancid easily; oxidised oil smells fishy, may lose its benefit, and many flavoured oils fail the limit.
omega_3_supplement.source: GOED Monograph (PV <=5 meq/kg, p-AV <=20, TOTOX <=26) https://goedomega3.com/storage/app/media/Monograph/GOED%20Monograph%20-%202026%2007%2023%20version%209.0.pdf; Trustified Kreis test; GWU 2023 rancidity study https://hsrc.himmelfarb.gwu.edu/gwhpubs/3398

omega_3_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
omega_3_supplement.why: Fish oils can carry mercury and arsenic from the sea if not purified properly.
omega_3_supplement.source: GOED Monograph (Cd, Hg, inorganic As <0.1 mg/kg); FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1; Unbox Health tests all four (29 reports)

packaged_food.name: Nutrition vs label claims
packaged_food.why: Checks that the nutrition table on the pack matches what's actually inside.

packaged_food.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
packaged_food.why: Metals from soil, water or processing build up in the body over years; FSSAI caps them in every food.
packaged_food.source: FSSAI Contaminants, Toxins and Residues Regulations 2011, Reg 2.1

packaged_food.name: Aflatoxins
packaged_food.why: Toxins from mould on grains, nuts and seeds; long-term exposure damages the liver.

packaged_food.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
packaged_food.why: Bacteria from poor hygiene or storage can cause food poisoning.
packaged_food.source: FSSAI FPS Regulations, Appendix B (microbiological standards)

paneer.name: Moisture and milk fat (dry-matter basis)
paneer.why: Extra water adds weight you pay for, and low fat means skimmed milk was used; FSSAI caps moisture at 60% and needs 50% fat on dry matter for full-fat paneer.
paneer.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.1.16 (chhana/paneer composition) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Draft_WTO_SPS_Notification_Standards_Diary_26_04_2018.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

paneer.name: Analogue check (vegetable oil, starch)
paneer.why: 'Analogue' paneer made with palm oil and starch is widely sold as real paneer; Maharashtra banned it in 2026 after 35% of samples failed and FSSAI has proposed a national ban.
paneer.source: FSSAI DART / Check Adulteration at Home: https://fssai.gov.in/cms/checkadulteration.php (starch in paneer: iodine test); FSSAI 2026 draft to bar 'paneer' name on analogues: https://www.moneylife.in/article/analogue-paneer-after-statelevel-bans-fssai-proposes-nationwide-curbs-on-nonmilk-products/81757.html

paneer.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
paneer.why: Paneer is moist and often handled by hand, so coliforms, yeast/mould and pathogens grow fast if hygiene or cold chain fails.
paneer.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B; Consumer Voice paneer microbiology tests: https://consumer-voice.org/paneer/packaged-paneer/

paneer.name: Nutrition vs label claims
paneer.why: High-protein paneer claims are common; tests check protein, calcium and energy really match the pack.
paneer.source: Unbox Health label-accuracy tests; Consumer Voice tests

paneer.name: Aflatoxin M1 (from mouldy cattle feed)
paneer.why: Aflatoxin M1 binds to milk protein, so it concentrates in paneer made from contaminated milk.
paneer.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (Aflatoxin M1 in milk 0.5 µg/kg); Trustified tests

paneer.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
paneer.why: Metals from contaminated milk, water or equipment accumulate in the body over time.
paneer.source: FSSAI CTR Regs 2011 (compendium): https://jaivikbharat.fssai.gov.in/pdf/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations.pdf (Reg 2.1: lead 0.02 mg/kg in secondary milk products); Unbox Health tests

peanut_butter.name: Aflatoxins
peanut_butter.why: Groundnuts are India's highest-risk crop for aflatoxins, which damage the liver and can cause cancer.
peanut_butter.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (products containing nuts/oilseeds: total 20 µg/kg, B1 10 µg/kg); Unbox Health and Trustified tests

peanut_butter.name: Nutrition vs label claims
peanut_butter.why: Checks protein, sugar and fat against the label, since many 'high protein' spreads add sugar and cheaper oil.

peanut_butter.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
peanut_butter.why: Groundnuts take up cadmium and lead from soil.
peanut_butter.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits); Unbox Health peanut butter tests

peanut_butter.name: Trans fat (FSSAI 2% of fat limit)
peanut_butter.why: Some peanut butters add hydrogenated oil to stop oil separating, which can add trans fat.
peanut_butter.source: FSSAI trans fat limit (industrial TFA ≤2% of fat) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/advisories/2021/12/61c0659e591e2Letter_Compliance_Trans_Fat_20_12_2021.pdf; Unbox Health peanut butter tests

pickle.name: Mould and yeast
pickle.why: A pickle must show no sign of fermentation; mould or yeast growth means spoilage and possible toxin formation.
pickle.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.43(1)-(2) and Appendix B (fermented/pickled fruit & vegetables: yeast & mould, Salmonella, Listeria) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf; Consumer Voice tests

pickle.name: Synthetic colours and mineral acid
pickle.why: Pickles must not contain synthetic dyes, mineral acid or alum, which are used to fake colour, sourness and crunch.

pickle.name: Preservatives (benzoic acid, sulphur dioxide)
pickle.why: Preservatives are allowed only up to set limits; overuse can cause reactions in sensitive people.
pickle.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix A (pickled fruits & vegetables) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20A(4).pdf

pickle.name: Salt, acidity and drained weight
pickle.why: Too little salt or acid lets germs grow, and low drained weight means you are paying for oil or brine instead of fruit and vegetables.
pickle.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.43(2) (drained weight ≥60%, NaCl ≥12% in brine, acidity ≥1.2% citric / ≥2% acetic) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_3_Fruit_Vegetable_products.pdf

pickle.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
pickle.why: Spices, oil and tin containers can bring lead and tin into pickles.
pickle.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1.1 (lead: pickled cucumbers 1.0 ppm, foods not specified 2.5 ppm; tin: pickled cucumber 250 ppm) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf

pre_workout.name: Banned stimulants (DMAA, DMHA, DMBA)
pre_workout.why: Pre-workouts have repeatedly been caught with hidden amphetamine-like stimulants that can cause heart problems and fail doping tests.
pre_workout.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 47 (no WADA-prohibited substances in sports foods) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; NSF/Cohen 2017 study https://www.nsf.org/news/banned-and-potentially-harmful-stimulants-found-in-six-supplements

pre_workout.name: Caffeine vs label
pre_workout.why: Too much caffeine per scoop can cause palpitations and anxiety; FSSAI caps caffeine in supplements.
pre_workout.source: FSSAI caffeine limits for food supplements https://www.foodresearchlab.com/insights/regulation-updates/what-are-the-fssai-regulations-for-caffeine-added-to-food-supplements/

pre_workout.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
pre_workout.why: Key ingredients like beta-alanine and citrulline are often under-dosed or hidden in 'proprietary blends'.
pre_workout.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

pre_workout.name: Banned substances (steroids, WADA-listed stimulants)
pre_workout.why: Gym products have been caught with hidden steroids or stimulants that are unsafe and can get athletes banned.
pre_workout.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 39 (no hormones, steroids, psychotropics) and FAQ 47 (no WADA-prohibited substances in sports foods) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf

pre_workout.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
pre_workout.why: Daily powders can carry heavy metals from raw materials and fillers.
pre_workout.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

protein_bar.name: Nutrition vs label claims
protein_bar.why: Bars are often short on protein and higher in sugar or fat than the label says.
protein_bar.source: FSSAI Labelling & Display Regs 2020 (nutrition info); Citizens Protein Project https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10994440/; Unbox Health bar/snack testing

protein_bar.name: Amino spiking (free amino acids, non-protein nitrogen)
protein_bar.why: Cheap amino acids like glycine or taurine can be added to fool the standard nitrogen test into showing more protein than is really there.
protein_bar.source: Trustified (41 reports) and Labdoor (free amino acids) test it; Kjeldahl/Dumas protein methods measure nitrogen, not protein

protein_bar.name: Aflatoxins
protein_bar.why: Nuts, peanuts and dates in bars are classic sources of aflatoxin, a liver-damaging mould toxin.
protein_bar.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2 (aflatoxin limits for nuts, groundnuts); Trustified tests it

protein_bar.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
protein_bar.why: Cocoa and plant proteins in bars are known to carry lead and cadmium.
protein_bar.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1; Unbox Health tests bars for all four

protein_bar.name: Pesticide residues
protein_bar.why: Oats, nuts and plant proteins can bring pesticide residues into the bar.
protein_bar.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3; Trustified tests it

protein_chip.name: Nutrition vs label claims
protein_chip.why: 'High protein' chips are often mostly starch and fat, so protein, fat and sodium need checking against the pack.
protein_chip.source: FSSAI Labelling & Display Regs 2020; Unbox Health tests protein, fat, sodium, sugar, fibre

protein_chip.name: Trans fat
protein_chip.why: Partly hydrogenated fats raise heart risk; FSSAI caps industrial trans fat at 2% of total fat.
protein_chip.source: FSSAI trans-fat limit (max 2% of fat, in force Jan 2022); Unbox Health tests trans fat on snack bars and protein chips

protein_chip.name: Rancidity (acid value, peroxide value)
protein_chip.why: Fried or baked chips made with stale or reused oil turn rancid, which tastes off and forms harmful oxidation products.
protein_chip.source: FSSAI draft namkeen standard (peroxide value <=10 meq/kg, acid value <=1.0 of extracted fat); IS 12566 extruded snacks

protein_chip.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
protein_chip.why: Pulse and grain flours can carry lead and cadmium from soil.
protein_chip.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1; Unbox Health tests all four

protein_milkshake.name: Nutrition vs label claims
protein_milkshake.why: Ready-to-drink shakes can be lower in protein and higher in sugar than the label claims.
protein_milkshake.source: FSSAI Labelling & Display Regs 2020; Unbox Health tests protein, sugar and full amino profile (5 reports)

protein_milkshake.name: Amino spiking (free amino acids, non-protein nitrogen)
protein_milkshake.why: Cheap amino acids like glycine or taurine can be added to fool the standard nitrogen test into showing more protein than is really there.
protein_milkshake.source: Trustified (41 reports) and Labdoor (free amino acids) test it; Kjeldahl/Dumas protein methods measure nitrogen, not protein

protein_milkshake.name: Aflatoxins
protein_milkshake.why: Aflatoxin M1 passes from mouldy cattle feed into milk, the main ingredient of these shakes.
protein_milkshake.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2 (aflatoxin M1 in milk 0.5 ug/kg); Unbox Health tests total aflatoxins M1 and B,G

protein_milkshake.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
protein_milkshake.why: Milk, cocoa and added protein can carry lead and other metals.
protein_milkshake.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1; Unbox Health tests all four

protein_milkshake.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
protein_milkshake.why: A milk drink that is not properly heat-treated or sealed can grow harmful bacteria like Listeria and Salmonella.

protein_powder.name: Nutrition vs label claims
protein_powder.why: A 2024 study found about 70% of 36 Indian protein powders had less protein than the label said, some only half.
protein_powder.source: Citizens Protein Project, Medicine 2024 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10994440/; Unbox Health (48) and Labdoor (16) test protein

protein_powder.name: Amino spiking (free amino acids, non-protein nitrogen)
protein_powder.why: Cheap amino acids like glycine or taurine can be added to fool the standard nitrogen test into showing more protein than is really there.
protein_powder.source: Trustified (41 reports) and Labdoor (free amino acids) test it; Kjeldahl/Dumas protein methods measure nitrogen, not protein

protein_powder.name: Melamine
protein_powder.why: Melamine is a nitrogen-rich industrial chemical that has been used to fake protein content in milk proteins, and it damages the kidneys.
protein_powder.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (melamine limit 2.5 mg/kg in food); Trustified tests it (39 reports)

protein_powder.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
protein_powder.why: Protein powders, especially plant-based ones, often carry lead and cadmium from soil; 75% of samples in the Indian study had lead.
protein_powder.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1; Citizens Protein Project https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10994440/; Unbox Health (48) and Labdoor (16)

protein_powder.name: Aflatoxins
protein_powder.why: Mould toxins from badly stored milk, soy or grain proteins can damage the liver; 14% of Indian samples had aflatoxins.
protein_powder.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2; Citizens Protein Project https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10994440/; Trustified (35) and Unbox Health (48)

protein_powder.name: Pesticide residues
protein_powder.why: Plant proteins (pea, rice, soy) can carry farm pesticide residues into a product eaten daily.
protein_powder.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3; Trustified (36 reports); Citizens Protein Project found residues only in plant-based products https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10994440/

protein_powder.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
protein_powder.why: Powders mixed into milk or water and not cooked must be free of germs like Salmonella and E. coli.
protein_powder.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B; Labdoor tests TPC, yeast/mould, coliforms, E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria (16 reports)

ready_to_eat.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
ready_to_eat.why: Retort-pouch and canned meals must be commercially sterile; a poor seal or under-processing lets dangerous bacteria grow at room temperature.
ready_to_eat.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.3.4 thermally processed curried vegetables / ready to eat https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_3_Fruit_Vegetable_products.pdf and Appendix B (thermally processed: commercial sterility) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf

ready_to_eat.name: Nutrition vs label claims
ready_to_eat.why: Ready meals are often high in fat and salt; tests check fat, sodium and energy against the label.

ready_to_eat.name: Trans fat (FSSAI 2% of fat limit)
ready_to_eat.why: Ready meals cooked with vanaspati or hydrogenated fats can carry trans fat.
ready_to_eat.source: FSSAI trans fat limit (industrial TFA ≤2% of fat) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/advisories/2021/12/61c0659e591e2Letter_Compliance_Trans_Fat_20_12_2021.pdf; Consumer Voice ready-to-eat tests

rice.name: Basmati authenticity (non-basmati mix, grain length, elongation)
rice.why: Cheaper non-basmati rice is mixed into basmati; FSSAI allows at most 15% and sets minimum grain length and cooked elongation.
rice.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.6(26) Basmati rice https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf; Consumer Voice basmati tests

rice.name: Grain quality: broken, damaged, chalky grains, foreign matter, uric acid
rice.why: Too many broken, damaged or chalky grains, stones or insect contamination (uric acid) means you are paying for poor-grade rice.
rice.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.6(24) rice and 2.4.6(26) basmati https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf

rice.name: Aflatoxins
rice.why: Rice stored damp grows moulds that make aflatoxins, which harm the liver.
rice.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (total aflatoxins 15 µg/kg, B1 10 µg/kg in cereals; 20 µg/kg in products containing them); Consumer Voice and Trustified rice tests

rice.name: Pesticide residues
rice.why: Paddy is heavily sprayed (e.g. tricyclazole), and FSSAI sets many rice-specific residue limits.
rice.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3.1 (rice MRLs); FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.6(1)

rice.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
rice.why: Rice absorbs cadmium, lead and arsenic from paddy soil and water more than most grains.
rice.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits) (cadmium 0.4 mg/kg polished rice, lead 0.2 mg/kg cereal grains)

rice.name: Added colour or polishing agents
rice.why: Sella and basmati rice are sometimes coloured (e.g. with turmeric) or polished to look better, which FSSAI does not allow.
rice.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.6(26) (basmati free from artificial colouring and polishing agents) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf; FSSAI DART tests 15-16

salt.name: Purity: sodium chloride, water-insoluble matter, moisture
salt.why: Salt bulked with chalk, grit or excess water has less sodium chloride and more insoluble matter than FSSAI allows.
salt.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.9.30 (NaCl ≥96% dry, insoluble ≤1%, moisture ≤6%) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_9_Salt_Spices_Condiments%20and%20related%20products.pdf; FSSAI DART test 28

salt.name: Iodine content (iodised salt)
salt.why: Iodised salt is India's main source of iodine; too little means the salt doesn't prevent goitre and thyroid problems.
salt.source: FSS (Fortification of Foods) Regulations, 2018; FSSAI DART test 36; Consumer Voice salt tests

salt.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
salt.why: Sea and lake salt can carry lead, arsenic, cadmium and mercury from contaminated water.
salt.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits) (salt: lead 2.0, cadmium 0.5, mercury 0.1 mg/kg); Consumer Voice salt tests (lead, arsenic)

sea_buckthorn_oil.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
sea_buckthorn_oil.why: The value is in its omega-7 (palmitoleic acid) and other fatty acids; cheap oils can be blended in and the profile will show it.
sea_buckthorn_oil.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health fatty-acid profile and vitamin E

sea_buckthorn_oil.name: Rancidity (acid value, peroxide value)
sea_buckthorn_oil.why: A berry oil full of unsaturated fats goes rancid quickly if stored or packed badly.
sea_buckthorn_oil.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.2 oil quality parameters (acid value, peroxide value)

sea_buckthorn_oil.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
sea_buckthorn_oil.why: Berry oils and their extraction can carry heavy metals.
sea_buckthorn_oil.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

shilajit_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
shilajit_supplement.why: Raw shilajit is a rock exudate naturally loaded with metals; poorly purified products can have high lead or arsenic.
shilajit_supplement.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia limits for herbal/mineral material (lead 10, arsenic 3, cadmium 0.3, mercury 1 ppm); Unbox Health tests all four (6 reports); review https://ijapr.in/index.php/ijapr/article/download/3272/2875

shilajit_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
shilajit_supplement.why: Fulvic acid is the main claimed active, and fake or diluted resins carry much less than labelled.
shilajit_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests fulvic acid (6 reports); note no official IP/API shilajit monograph

shilajit_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
shilajit_supplement.why: Shilajit is a raw natural resin and can carry soil germs if not purified.
shilajit_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

snack_bar.name: Nutrition vs label claims
snack_bar.why: Snack and 'healthy' bars often hide more sugar and less fibre or protein than the label shows.
snack_bar.source: FSSAI Labelling & Display Regs 2020; Unbox Health tests full nutrition panel (13 reports)

snack_bar.name: Aflatoxins
snack_bar.why: Nuts, peanuts, seeds and dates are high-risk for aflatoxin, a mould toxin that harms the liver.
snack_bar.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2; Unbox Health tests total aflatoxins (13 reports)

snack_bar.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
snack_bar.why: Cocoa, seeds and grains in bars can carry lead and cadmium.
snack_bar.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1; Unbox Health tests all four (13 reports)

snack_bar.name: Trans fat
snack_bar.why: Partly hydrogenated fats raise heart risk; FSSAI caps industrial trans fat at 2% of total fat.
snack_bar.source: FSSAI trans-fat limit (max 2% of fat, in force Jan 2022); Unbox Health tests trans fat on snack bars and protein chips

snacks.name: Rancidity (acid value, peroxide value)
snacks.why: Namkeen fried in reused or old oil goes rancid, which tastes off and makes harmful oxidised fats.
snacks.source: Consumer Voice namkeen/snack tests (acid value and peroxide value of extracted fat); FSSAI FPS Reg 2.12.1 proprietary food https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/13_%20Chapter%202_12%20(Proprietary%20Food).pdf

snacks.name: Mineral oil
snacks.why: Cheap non-edible mineral oil is sometimes used in frying or added for shine; it is not a food oil.

snacks.name: Trans fat (FSSAI 2% of fat limit)
snacks.why: Snacks fried in vanaspati or partially hydrogenated oil can carry trans fat, which raises heart-disease risk.
snacks.source: FSSAI trans fat limit (industrial TFA ≤2% of fat, products made from 1 Jan 2022) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/advisories/2021/12/61c0659e591e2Letter_Compliance_Trans_Fat_20_12_2021.pdf

snacks.name: Nutrition vs label claims
snacks.why: Namkeen is high in salt and fat; tests check sodium, fat and energy against the label.

snacks.name: Purity: ash insoluble in HCl
snacks.why: High acid-insoluble ash means sand or grit in the besan, dal or other flours.

snacks.name: Aflatoxins
snacks.why: Namkeen is full of groundnuts, besan and dal, all prone to aflatoxin-producing moulds.
snacks.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (food products containing nuts, oilseeds, cereals or pulses: 20 µg/kg)

snacks.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
snacks.why: Snacks packed by hand after frying can pick up bacteria; proprietary foods must be free of pathogens.
snacks.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.12.1(4) proprietary food https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/13_%20Chapter%202_12%20(Proprietary%20Food).pdf; Consumer Voice snack tests

soya_chunks.name: Protein & composition (FSSAI soy chunk standard)
soya_chunks.why: Soya chunks are bought for protein; FSSAI requires at least 50% protein with limits on fat, ash and fibre.
soya_chunks.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.4.27 Textured Soy Protein https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_4_Cereals_and_Cereal_products.pdf

soya_chunks.name: Aflatoxins
soya_chunks.why: Soybeans stored damp grow moulds that make aflatoxins, which harm the liver.
soya_chunks.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (oilseeds 15 µg/kg, products containing them 20 µg/kg); Trustified tests

soya_chunks.name: Hexane residue (solvent)
soya_chunks.why: Soya chunks are made from solvent-extracted soy flour, and leftover hexane solvent must stay under 10 ppm.

soya_chunks.name: Pesticide residues
soya_chunks.why: Soybean crops are sprayed and residues can carry through to the chunks.

soya_chunks.name: Urease activity (under-processed soy)
soya_chunks.why: High urease means the soy wasn't heated enough to destroy anti-nutrients that block protein digestion.

spices.name: Aflatoxins
spices.why: Chillies, turmeric and coriander dried in the open grow moulds that make aflatoxins, which damage the liver.
spices.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.2.1 (spices: total aflatoxins 30 µg/kg, B1 15 µg/kg); Trustified and Consumer Voice spice tests

spices.name: Pesticide residues
spices.why: Spices carry pesticide and fumigant residues; in 2024 ethylene oxide, a cancer-causing fumigant, got Indian masalas recalled abroad and FSSAI testing them (ask the lab to include ethylene oxide).
spices.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3.1; Trustified spice tests; FSSAI ethylene oxide testing 2024 https://www.theweek.in/news/india/2024/05/21/fssai-clears-mdh-everest-spices-samples-finds-no-trace-of-ethylene-oxide.amp.html

spices.name: Synthetic colours (Sudan dyes, metanil yellow)
spices.why: Chilli and turmeric powders are dyed brighter with banned industrial dyes such as Sudan red and metanil yellow, which are linked to cancer.
spices.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.9.3 (chilli powder free of extraneous colour) and 2.9.18 (turmeric) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_9_Salt_Spices_Condiments%20and%20related%20products.pdf; FSSAI DART tests 24, 34; Trustified spice tests

spices.name: Lead chromate (turmeric colouring)
spices.why: Turmeric is sometimes coloured with lead chromate, a toxic lead pigment; FSSAI requires the test to be negative.
spices.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.9.18 (test for lead chromate: negative) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_9_Salt_Spices_Condiments%20and%20related%20products.pdf; FSSAI DART test 33; FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead in turmeric 10 mg/kg)

spices.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
spices.why: Lead from colouring, soil and grinding builds up in the body; FSSAI caps lead at 10 mg/kg in turmeric and curry powder.
spices.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits); FSSAI FPS Reg 2.9.19 curry powder (lead ≤10 ppm); Consumer Voice spice tests (lead)

spices.name: Purity: ash insoluble in HCl, volatile oil, curcumin, starch
spices.why: Brick powder, sand or sawdust in ground spices shows as high acid-insoluble ash, while low volatile oil or curcumin means exhausted or diluted spice.
spices.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.9 (per-spice limits, e.g. 2.9.3, 2.9.7, 2.9.18, 2.9.20 mixed masala) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_9_Salt_Spices_Condiments%20and%20related%20products.pdf; FSSAI DART tests 26, 35

spices.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
spices.why: Spices are dried outdoors and eaten without cooking in chutneys and raitas, so Salmonella must be absent.
spices.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B Table 3 (spices: Salmonella absent/25 g, B. cereus, Enterobacteriaceae) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf; Trustified and Consumer Voice tests

supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
supplement.why: Supplements are often short on the ingredient they are sold for; FSSAI allows only 10% below the label.
supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health/Labdoor label-accuracy testing; Consumer Voice tests

supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
supplement.why: Minerals, herbs and fillers in supplements are common sources of lead, arsenic, cadmium and mercury.
supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
supplement.why: Tablets, powders and gummies can pick up germs in manufacturing.
supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Consumer Voice tests Salmonella and Listeria; Labdoor tests

sweets.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
sweets.why: Milk sweets like rasgulla and peda spoil fast and can carry Staph aureus, coliforms and E. coli from handling.
sweets.source: FSSAI FPS Appendix B Table 1 (chhena-based and khoa-based sweets) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Appendix%20B(1).pdf; Consumer Voice sweets tests

sweets.name: Synthetic colours
sweets.why: Sweets are often coloured with non-permitted dyes or more than the legal limit of permitted colours.
sweets.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 3.1.2 / Appendix A (permitted synthetic colours, max 100 ppm in sweets)

sweets.name: Silver leaf (aluminium)
sweets.why: Chandi varq on sweets is sometimes cheap aluminium foil; FSSAI requires 99.9% pure silver.
sweets.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.11.4 silver leaf https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/12_%20Chapter%202_11%20(Other%20food%20product%20and%20%20ingredients).pdf; FSSAI DART test 10

sweets.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
sweets.why: Colours, silver leaf and utensils can add lead and other metals to sweets.
sweets.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury limits); Consumer Voice sweets tests (lead, arsenic)

sweets.name: Starch in khoa / chhena
sweets.why: Khoa and chhena are bulked with starch, so you get less milk solids than you pay for.
sweets.source: FSSAI DART test 3 (starch in khoa, chhena, paneer) https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/knowledge_hub/1878035b34b558a3b48DART%20Book.pdf

sweets.name: Trans fat (FSSAI 2% of fat limit)
sweets.why: Soan papdi and fried sweets are often made with vanaspati, a source of trans fat.
sweets.source: FSSAI trans fat limit (industrial TFA ≤2% of fat) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/advisories/2021/12/61c0659e591e2Letter_Compliance_Trans_Fat_20_12_2021.pdf; Consumer Voice sweets tests

sweets.name: Nutrition vs label claims
sweets.why: Checks sugar, fat and energy against the label.

tea.name: Pesticide residues
tea.why: Tea leaves are sprayed heavily and are not washed before brewing, and FSSAI and the Tea Board keep finding samples above residue limits.
tea.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.3.1 (tea-specific MRLs for dozens of pesticides) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; FSSAI direction to labs on pesticide testing in tea, 04.03.2024 https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/advisories/2024/03/65e6f53962cfbDirection_04.03.2024.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

tea.name: Added synthetic colour
tea.why: Dyes like tartrazine are used to make low-grade or used tea give a strong colour; any added colour is banned in tea.
tea.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.10.1(1) (free from added colouring matter) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_10_BEVERAGES_Other%20than%20Dairy%20and%20Fruits%20Vegetables%20based.pdf; FSSAI DART (coloured tea) https://www.fssai.gov.in/book-details.php?bkid=201; Tea Board anti-adulteration campaign 2026; Consumer Voice tests

tea.name: Iron filings
tea.why: Iron dust from processing machines, or added to bulk up weight, ends up in the tea; FSSAI caps it at 125 mg/kg.
tea.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.10.1(1)(g) (iron filings ≤125 mg/kg) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_10_BEVERAGES_Other%20than%20Dairy%20and%20Fruits%20Vegetables%20based.pdf; FSSAI DART https://www.fssai.gov.in/book-details.php?bkid=201; Consumer Voice tests

tea.name: Purity: ash, water extract, crude fibre
tea.why: These show whether the pack is real tea leaf or padded with used (exhausted) tea, stalks, sand or dust.
tea.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.10.1(1)(a)-(f) (total ash 4–8%, water-soluble ash ≥45%, acid-insoluble ash ≤1%, water extract ≥32%, crude fibre ≤16.5%) https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_10_BEVERAGES_Other%20than%20Dairy%20and%20Fruits%20Vegetables%20based.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

tea.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
tea.why: Tea plants take up lead and copper from soil and sprays; FSSAI caps lead at 5 ppm and copper at 150 ppm in tea.
tea.source: FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1.1 (tea: lead 5.0 ppm, copper 150 ppm) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations_20_08_2020.pdf; Consumer Voice tests (lead, copper)

tea.name: Aflatoxins
tea.why: Damp storage can let moulds grow on tea and produce liver-damaging aflatoxins.
tea.source: Consumer Voice tests (aflatoxins in 14 tea reports); Trustified tests

vanaspati.name: Trans fat
vanaspati.why: Partially hydrogenated fat is the biggest source of trans fat, which raises heart-disease risk; FSSAI has capped it at 2% since 2022.
vanaspati.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.2.6 (vanaspati: trans fat ≤2% from 1.1.2022) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_2_Fats_oil_fat%20emulsions.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

vanaspati.name: Nickel (hydrogenation catalyst)
vanaspati.why: Nickel used to harden the oil can stay in the product; FSSAI allows at most 1.5 ppm.
vanaspati.source: FSSAI CTR Regs 2011 (compendium): https://jaivikbharat.fssai.gov.in/pdf/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations.pdf (Reg 2.1: nickel 1.5 mg/kg in hydrogenated oils); FSSAI FPS Reg 2.2.6

vanaspati.name: Sesame oil marker (Baudouin test) and vitamin A
vanaspati.why: By law vanaspati must contain sesame oil so it can be detected if mixed into ghee, plus at least 25 IU/g vitamin A.
vanaspati.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.2.6(v) and (vii) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_2_Fats_oil_fat%20emulsions.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

vanaspati.name: Argemone oil and animal fat adulteration
vanaspati.why: Toxic argemone oil or cheap animal fat can be mixed into the base oils; FSSAI requires argemone to be absent.
vanaspati.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.2.6 (argemone negative) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_2_Fats_oil_fat%20emulsions.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

vanaspati.name: Rancidity (acid value, peroxide value)
vanaspati.why: Stale or badly refined fat has high acid and peroxide values; FSSAI caps the acid value at 0.6.
vanaspati.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.2.6 (acid value ≤0.6) and 2.2.8 (peroxide value) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_2_Fats_oil_fat%20emulsions.pdf

vanaspati.name: Purity: unsaponifiable matter, refractive index, moisture
vanaspati.why: These check the fat was made from approved refined oils and isn't padded with water or non-fat matter.
vanaspati.source: FSSAI FPS Reg 2.2.6 (moisture ≤0.25%, unsaponifiable ≤2%) https://mail.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_2_Fats_oil_fat%20emulsions.pdf; Consumer Voice tests

vegan_collagen.name: Collagen identity (hydroxyproline, glycine, proline)
vegan_collagen.why: Collagen only comes from animals; plant 'collagen' has almost no hydroxyproline, so this test shows whether it resembles collagen at all.

vegan_collagen.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
vegan_collagen.why: These are usually plant protein, amino acid and vitamin blends, and the claimed amounts need checking.
vegan_collagen.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

vegan_collagen.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
vegan_collagen.why: Plant proteins and herbal extracts in these blends often carry lead and cadmium.
vegan_collagen.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

vegan_collagen.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
vegan_collagen.why: Plant-based powders can carry field germs if not cleaned properly.
vegan_collagen.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

vitamin_b12_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
vitamin_b12_supplement.why: B12 doses are tiny (micrograms), so small manufacturing errors leave products well short of the label.
vitamin_b12_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

vitamin_b12_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
vitamin_b12_supplement.why: Tablets and sprays can carry heavy metals from fillers.
vitamin_b12_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

vitamin_b12_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
vitamin_b12_supplement.why: Sprays, drops and gummies can grow germs if made badly.
vitamin_b12_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

vitamin_c_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
vitamin_c_supplement.why: Vitamin C breaks down with heat, light and moisture, so many products have less than the label says by the time you take them.
vitamin_c_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

vitamin_c_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
vitamin_c_supplement.why: Effervescent and chewable forms use salts and fillers that can carry lead or arsenic.
vitamin_c_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

vitamin_c_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
vitamin_c_supplement.why: Chewables and gummies are sugary and can grow mould or bacteria if made badly.
vitamin_c_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

vitamin_d_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
vitamin_d_supplement.why: Too little vitamin D does nothing and too much builds up in the body and can raise blood calcium dangerously, so dose accuracy matters.
vitamin_d_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (-10% tolerance) and Schedule I upper limits https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests (10 reports)

vitamin_d_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
vitamin_d_supplement.why: Capsule oils and fillers can carry heavy metals.
vitamin_d_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

vitamin_d_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
vitamin_d_supplement.why: Drops, gummies and sachets can pick up germs in manufacturing.
vitamin_d_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B

vitamin_k2_supplement.name: Active ingredient vs label claim
vitamin_k2_supplement.why: K2 (MK-7) is expensive and unstable, so products are often short on it; many also claim vitamin D3 that needs checking.
vitamin_k2_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 25 (no more than 10% below declared value) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health tests

vitamin_k2_supplement.name: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury)
vitamin_k2_supplement.why: Fermented or plant-sourced K2 and its oil carriers can carry heavy metals.
vitamin_k2_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 76 (products must meet FSSAI CTR Reg 2.1 metal limits) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; Unbox Health and Labdoor test all four

vitamin_k2_supplement.name: Microbiology (E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria)
vitamin_k2_supplement.why: Capsules and tablets can pick up germs in manufacturing.
vitamin_k2_supplement.source: FSSAI Nutra FAQ 77 (tested for basic indicator organisms) https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FAQs_Nutraceutical_Regulations_06_10_2020.pdf; FSSAI FPS Appendix B
